ses.title: Connect your AWS SES
ses.subtitle: Your instance sends through your own SES account.

setup.cliNote: Run pnpm setup:aws from a clone of this repo — or docker compose run --rm millionsend setup on the server. It runs with YOUR AWS credentials, creates everything, and prints the .env lines to paste if MillionSend runs elsewhere.
setup.scriptNote: Paste into a terminal where the AWS CLI has admin credentials. It creates the IAM user, policy, SNS topic, and configuration set, then prints your .env lines.
setup.eventsSkipped: APP_BASE_URL is not a public https URL, so the event ingestion part is left out. Set it and reload to include it.
setup.cfnNote: One click: opens the CloudFormation review page with the hosted template — the same stack as infra/millionsend-ses.cfn.yaml. From a terminal instead:
setup.step1: Create a policy: IAM console → Policies → Create policy → JSON — paste this document.
setup.step2: Create a user named millionsend and attach the policy.
setup.step3: Create an access key for the user and paste it into .env.
setup.step4: Optional events: SNS topic + configuration set — the script above automates this part; see SELF_HOSTING.md.

credentials.title: Credentials
credentials.keysChain: not set — the default provider chain will be attempted
credentials.snsNote: not set — event ingestion is disabled
credentials.configSetNote: not set — SES publishes no events

test.title: Test connection
test.note: runs GetAccount from the instance — read-only, nothing is sent
test.sandboxTitle: Your SES account is in sandbox.
test.sandboxBody: Recipients must be verified until AWS grants production access.
test.requestTemplate:
Use case: transactional email (account notifications, receipts, password resets) sent through MillionSend, a self-hosted sending platform we operate on our own infrastructure.

Recipients: our own users. List subscriptions follow double-opt-in guidance before any sending.

Bounce and complaint handling: SES delivery events are ingested via SNS; hard bounces and complaints are suppressed automatically and are never mailed again.

Expected volume: [VOLUME] emails/day, ramping up gradually.
test.requestTemplateNote: Replace [VOLUME], then paste it into the AWS production access request form.
test.rateHint: SES_MAX_SEND_RATE={envRate} in .env · account max {accountRate}/s — these disagree.

errors.credentials: AWS rejected the credentials — check AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY in .env.
errors.unreachable: SES did not respond — check AWS_REGION and the network path.
